thread:
ashley: FYI — cost panel rollout v2 just hit canary and we're seeing route affinity churn. token-costs jumping on cached requests. anyone else?
sam: Yep, saw a 20% token bump in the canary window. looks tied to the new 'light-weight tokenization' flag.
jamie: I think the attribution path changed when we added the route demux. cache keys now include model_variant_id which breaks the cache lineage, so credits aren't applied.
olivia: Oof. So routes that should've been credited as cache hits are being billed as fresh generation?
sam: Exactly. logs show `cache.miss` but payloads look identical. snippet: ```json
{"model_variant":"m-v2","input_hash":"abc123"}
```
ashley: deploy-bot, when was the canary pushed?
deploy-bot: Canary rollout started 1731234500 by ci/cd (ashley). 3 instances.
lee: Quick thought — routing policy added a sticky token that rewrites the request id when falling back to cheaper model. that could alter cache key.
jamie: Yeah, the new routing header `x-route-affinity` gets appended to the request body before hashing. bug.
olivia: For rollout UX: can we make the cost delta visible in the console before full rollout? even a quick per-route diff would help.
ashley: Agree. For now can we patch the canary to strip the header before cache key calc?
sam: I can ship a patch to the runtime that ignores affinity headers when computing cache fingerprint. small PR incoming.
jamie: Also we should add an e2e test asserting cache credits preserved across model fallbacks.
ashley: Thanks. Sam, ping here when PR deploys. Olivia, can you add a console card to surface per-route token delta for canaries? just a preview widget.
olivia: Will do — adding to the canary dashboard card backlog.
ashley: Okay locking this thread — follow ups in the PR and dashboard ticket. :thumbsup:
